original_question: Does there exist a non-conformally flat metric on the sphere S n , n > 2, whose geodesic flow is maximally superintegrable (in the class of integrals which are polynomial in momenta)?
correct_elements: Your draft is already almost exactly the paper’s official formulation: it has the correct manifold (the sphere S^n with n>2), the correct geometric restriction (non-conformally flat metric), the correct dynamical object (the geodesic flow), and the correct notion of integrability (maximal superintegrability in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))
missing_details: The surrounding setup is Riemannian: the metric should be named as a Riemannian metric g on M=S^n. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))

To be fully stand-alone, the geodesic flow should be identified as the Hamiltonian flow on T^*S^n of H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j, with the canonical symplectic structure. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))

“Maximally superintegrable” should be unpacked as the existence of 2n-1 functionally independent first integrals (counting H), which is the maximal number for an n-dimensional manifold. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))

“Integrals which are polynomial in momenta” should be made explicit as first integrals polynomial in the fiber variables p, with smooth coefficients depending on x∈S^n. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))

If one wants the question completely explicit, the quantifier should be stated: the paper writes “on the sphere S^n, n>2”; a stand-alone sharpening should say whether this means existence for some integer n>2. The most conservative reading is existential: there exists n>2 and such a metric on S^n. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))

The surrounding definition of superintegrability also mentions the customary requirement that the common level sets of the integrals be isotropic submanifolds of T^*M; this is part of the nearby context even though the operative content of Question 3.11 is the 2n-1-integral count. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))
refined_question: Does there exist an integer n>2 and a non-conformally flat Riemannian metric g on S^n such that the geodesic Hamiltonian H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j on T^*S^n admits 2n-1 functionally independent first integrals, including H, each polynomial in the momenta p with smooth x-dependent coefficients?
justification: The draft clearly targets Question 3.11 in §3.2, not Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, because its wording matches that question almost verbatim. I therefore kept the scope exactly on higher-dimensional spheres and geodesic flows, without broadening to general natural Hamiltonian systems or arbitrary manifolds. The refinement only makes explicit the ambient phase space T^*S^n, the geodesic Hamiltonian H=1/2 g^{ij}p_i p_j from §3, and the definition of “maximally superintegrable” given immediately before Question 3.11. The surrounding text explains why the non-conformally-flat condition is the point of the question: in higher dimensions, the cited partial results concern conformally flat metrics, mainly in dimension 3 for quadratic integrals. I did not add any degree, homogeneity, field, or nilpotency restrictions, because none belong to this problem in the paper’s formulation. Although §3.1 notes the standard correspondence between polynomial first integrals of geodesic flows and Killing tensors, the paper does not restate Question 3.11 as a separately labeled equivalent formulation, so I left that field null. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/718695571/1804-03737))

surrounding text after equation (3.1): polynomial integrals are polynomial in momenta; in the geodesic-flow case they correspond to Killing tensors
definition of superintegrable and maximally superintegrable systems
